ex.en: They have no impact on the environment.
ex.zh: 它們對環境完全沒有影響。

ex.en: The blizzard has already had a severe impact on the economy.
ex.zh: 這場暴風雪已經對經濟造成嚴重衝擊。

ex.en: This incident has made a great impact on the progress of the project.
ex.zh: 這起事件大大影響了專案進度。

impact.en: a strong effect that something has on a person or thing

ex.en: Rising costs will impact our profits.
ex.zh: 成本上升會影響我們的獲利。

ex.en: The new policy impacted thousands of workers.
ex.zh: 新政策影響了數千名員工。

impact.en: to have a strong effect on something

ex.en: The car was badly damaged on impact.
ex.zh: 汽車在撞擊時嚴重受損。

ex.en: The phone case protects against impact.
ex.zh: 這個手機殼可以防撞。

impact.en: the force or act of one object hitting another

ex.en: It is imperative for you to act at once.
ex.zh: 你必須立刻採取行動。

ex.en: It is imperative for you to finish by Sunday.
ex.zh: 你一定要在星期日前完成。

ex.en: It is imperative that we meet the deadline.
ex.zh: 我們務必要趕上截止期限。

imperative.en: extremely important and needing to be done at once

ex.en: The longer we waited, the more impatient we became.
ex.zh: 我們等得越久，就越不耐煩。

ex.en: I think Tom is a bit too impatient.
ex.zh: 我覺得湯姆有點太沒耐心了。

impatient.en: annoyed because you have to wait or something is slow

ex.en: The kids are impatient to open their presents.
ex.zh: 孩子們迫不及待想拆禮物。

ex.en: She was impatient to start her new job.
ex.zh: 她迫不及待想開始新工作。

impatient.en: very eager to do something and unwilling to wait

ex.en: He has a hearing impairment.
ex.zh: 他有聽力障礙。

ex.en: Lack of sleep can cause memory impairment.
ex.zh: 睡眠不足會造成記憶力受損。

impairment.en: a problem that stops part of the body or mind from working well

ex.en: The company recorded an impairment loss on the old factory.
ex.zh: 公司就舊工廠認列了減損損失。

ex.en: The auditors asked about the asset impairment.
ex.zh: 會計師詢問了資產減損的情況。

impairment.en: a drop in the value of something a company owns, recorded in its accounts

implicit.zh: 暗示的、含蓄的、不言而喻的

ex.en: There was an implicit criticism in his comment.
ex.zh: 他的話裡隱含著批評。

ex.en: Her silence was an implicit agreement.
ex.zh: 她的沉默等於默許。

implicit.en: suggested or understood without being said directly

ex.en: I have implicit trust in my team.
ex.zh: 我完全信任我的團隊。

ex.en: She has implicit faith in her doctor.
ex.zh: 她對她的醫生深信不疑。

ex.en: The rules must be few and, more importantly, simple.
ex.zh: 規則要少，更重要的是要簡單。

ex.en: She's beautiful, smart, and - most importantly - has a good heart.
ex.zh: 她漂亮、聰明，而且最重要的是心地善良。

ex.en: One needs to do their best in all things, and more importantly work within their abilities.
ex.zh: 凡事要盡力而為，更重要的是要量力而行。

importantly.en: used to introduce a point that matters more than the others

ex.en: Everybody is immune to smallpox nowadays.
ex.zh: 現在大家都對天花免疫了。

ex.en: The immune system protects the body from disease.
ex.zh: 免疫系統保護身體不受疾病侵害。

immune.en: protected from a disease because the body can fight it

ex.en: No company is immune to an economic crisis.
ex.zh: 沒有一家公司能不受經濟危機影響。

ex.en: He seems immune to criticism.
ex.zh: 他似乎對批評無動於衷。

immune.en: not affected by something bad, or free from a rule or duty

ex.en: There is an imbalance between supply and demand.
ex.zh: 供需之間失衡。

ex.en: A trade imbalance can hurt the economy.
ex.zh: 貿易失衡可能會傷害經濟。

imbalance.en: a situation where things are not equal or fair

imminent.zh: 即將發生的、迫在眉睫的

ex.en: A decision on the merger is imminent.
ex.zh: 合併案即將做出決定。

ex.en: Dark clouds warned that a storm was imminent.
ex.zh: 烏雲預示暴風雨即將來臨。

impair.zh: 損害、削弱、影響（能力、功能）

ex.en: Lack of sleep can impair your judgment.
ex.zh: 睡眠不足會影響你的判斷力。

ex.en: Drinking alcohol impairs your ability to drive.
ex.zh: 喝酒會削弱你的駕駛能力。

ex.en: The app is designed for people with impaired vision.
ex.zh: 這個 App 是為視力受損的人設計的。

impair.en: to make something weaker or worse

ex.en: We are the largest importer of coffee in Taiwan.
ex.zh: 我們是台灣最大的咖啡進口商。

ex.en: The importer must pay duties on the goods.
ex.zh: 進口商必須為這批貨支付關稅。

importer.en: a person or company that buys goods from other countries

ex.en: Honesty was the most important factor in his success.
ex.zh: 誠實是他成功最重要的因素。

ex.en: Breakfast is the most important meal of the day.
ex.zh: 早飯是一天中最重要的一頓飯。

ex.en: It is important for him to get the job.
ex.zh: 得到那份工作對他來說很重要。

important.en: having great value or a strong effect on something

ex.en: I would like to improve my English pronunciation.
ex.zh: 我想改善我的英文發音。

ex.en: We are always looking for ways to improve our service.
ex.zh: 我們一直在尋找改善服務的方法。

ex.en: Tom's Japanese is improving little by little.
ex.zh: 湯姆的日文一點一點在進步。

ex.en: With her help, my French improved little by little.
ex.zh: 在她的幫助下，我的法文慢慢進步了。

ex.en: It has greatly improved compared with what it was.
ex.zh: 和以前相比，已經進步很多了。

ex.en: Today no one can imagine a life without television.
ex.zh: 現在沒有人能想像沒有電視的生活。

ex.en: He is not like the person I imagined.
ex.zh: 他跟我想像中的人不一樣。

ex.en: Imagine working from a beach in Bali.
ex.zh: 想像一下在峇里島的海灘上工作。

imagine.en: to form a picture or idea of something in your mind

ex.en: I foolishly imagined that he was going to help me.
ex.zh: 我傻傻地以為他會幫我。

ex.en: I imagine you must be tired after the flight.
ex.zh: 我想你搭完飛機一定很累吧。

imagine.en: to think or suppose that something is true

ex.en: It is necessary for you to go there immediately.
ex.zh: 你必須馬上去那裡。

ex.en: We took action immediately so that things wouldn't get worse.
ex.zh: 為了避免情況惡化，我們立刻採取了行動。

ex.en: He commanded me to leave the room immediately.
ex.zh: 他命令我立刻離開這個房間。

ex.en: He placed emphasis on the importance of education.
ex.zh: 他強調教育的重要性。

ex.en: I didn't realize the importance of that problem.
ex.zh: 我沒意識到那個問題的重要性。

ex.en: This is a matter of the utmost importance.
ex.zh: 這件事至關重要。

importance.en: the quality of being very useful, valuable or necessary

ex.en: We've made a lot of improvements today.
ex.zh: 我們今天有了很多進步。

ex.en: Actually, the present method has plenty of room for improvement.
ex.zh: 其實目前的方法還有很大的改善空間。

ex.en: Your essay still needs some improvement.
ex.zh: 你的論文還需要一些改進。

improvement.en: a change that makes something better

ex.en: It's impossible for me to explain it to you.
ex.zh: 我不可能解釋給你聽。

ex.en: Finishing the report by tomorrow is next to impossible.
ex.zh: 明天之前完成報告幾乎是不可能的。

ex.en: It is impossible to master English in a short time.
ex.zh: 不可能在短時間內精通英語。

impossible.en: not able to happen or be done

ex.en: My first impression of him proved to be correct.
ex.zh: 我對他的第一印象果然沒錯。

ex.en: What you said left a deep impression on me.
ex.zh: 你說的話讓我印象非常深刻。

ex.en: That day left a deep impression on me.
ex.zh: 那一天讓我印象很深刻。

impression.en: the feeling or opinion you form about someone or something

impression.zh: be under the impression that：以為、誤以為

ex.en: I was under the impression that the meeting was canceled.
ex.zh: 我原本以為會議取消了。

ex.en: She was under the impression that Tom was single.
ex.zh: 她一直以為湯姆是單身。

impression.en: to believe something that may not be true

ex.en: We should try to avoid imposing our own beliefs on others.
ex.zh: 我們應該盡量避免把自己的信念強加在別人身上。

ex.en: He always imposes his opinion on me.
ex.zh: 他總是把他的看法強加給我。

impose.en: to force your ideas or wishes on other people

ex.en: The government imposed a new tax on imported cars.
ex.zh: 政府對進口車課徵新稅。

ex.en: The city imposed strict rules on parking.
ex.zh: 市政府對停車實施嚴格規定。

impose.en: to officially introduce a tax, rule or limit

ex.en: I don't want to impose on you.
ex.zh: 我不想給你添麻煩。

ex.en: Are you sure I'm not imposing?
ex.zh: 你確定我不會打擾到你嗎？

impose.en: to ask too much of someone and cause them trouble

ex.en: They needed to make a decision - an immediate decision.
ex.zh: 他們需要做決定，而且是立刻做決定。

ex.en: His speech won the immediate applause of the audience.
ex.zh: 他的演講立刻贏得了觀眾的掌聲。

ex.en: The new policy will take immediate effect.
ex.zh: 新政策將立即生效。

immediate.en: happening or done at once, without delay

immediate.zh: 直接的；最接近的（如直屬主管、直系親屬）

ex.en: Please report any problems to your immediate supervisor.
ex.zh: 有任何問題請向你的直屬主管報告。

ex.en: Only immediate family members attended the wedding.
ex.zh: 只有直系親屬參加了婚禮。

ex.en: None of them could understand what she was implying.
ex.zh: 他們沒有人聽得懂她在暗示什麼。

ex.en: Are you implying that I'm too young?
ex.zh: 你是在暗示我太年輕嗎？

ex.en: I didn't mean to imply otherwise.
ex.zh: 我沒有要暗示別的意思。

imply.en: to suggest something without saying it directly

ex.en: A good education doesn't imply a good upbringing.
ex.zh: 受過良好教育不代表有良好的教養。

ex.en: A higher price doesn't necessarily imply better quality.
ex.zh: 價格較高不一定代表品質較好。

imply.en: to show that something is probably true or has to be true

ex.en: This will have enormous implications for Algeria.
ex.zh: 這將對阿爾及利亞產生重大影響。

ex.en: We need to consider the implications of this decision.
ex.zh: 我們必須考慮這個決定可能帶來的影響。

implication.en: an effect or result that something may have later

ex.en: The implication was that where there was a well, there were residents.
ex.zh: 言下之意是，有水井的地方就有人居住。

ex.en: By implication, he was blaming his manager.
ex.zh: 他的話暗指是主管的錯。

implication.en: something that is suggested but not said directly

ex.en: We were deeply impressed by the lecturer's eloquent speech.
ex.zh: 演講者精彩的演說讓我們印象深刻。

ex.en: Tom's designs didn't impress me much.
ex.zh: 湯姆的設計沒讓我覺得有多厲害。

ex.en: I couldn't help but be impressed by Tom's courage.
ex.zh: 湯姆的勇氣讓我不得不佩服。

impress.en: to make people feel great respect or admiration

impressive.zh: 令人印象深刻的、出色的

ex.en: I find her very impressive.
ex.zh: 我覺得她很令人佩服。

ex.en: You've both been very impressive today. I'm proud of you.
ex.zh: 你們兩個今天都表現得很出色。我以你們為傲。

ex.en: The company's growth this year is impressive.
ex.zh: 公司今年的成長令人印象深刻。

impressive.en: causing admiration because of great quality or size

ex.en: We are encouraged to use our imagination.
ex.zh: 我們被鼓勵發揮想像力。

ex.en: Imagination affects every aspect of our lives.
ex.zh: 想像力影響著我們生活的各個方面。

ex.en: I want you to use your imagination.
ex.zh: 我希望你發揮自己的想像力。

imagination.en: the ability to make pictures or new ideas in your mind

ex.en: This is beyond the scope of my imagination.
ex.zh: 這超出了我的想像。

ex.en: Don't worry, it's just your imagination.
ex.zh: 別擔心，那只是你的想像。

imagination.en: something that exists only in your mind and is not real

ex.en: Many of the immigrants changed their names.
ex.zh: 許多移民改了名字。

ex.en: Most Americans are descended from immigrants.
ex.zh: 大多數美國人都是移民的後代。

ex.en: America is a land of immigrants.
ex.zh: 美國是一個移民國家。

immigrant.en: a person who comes to live permanently in a foreign country

ex.en: The implementation of the new system will take six months.
ex.zh: 新系統的導入需要六個月。

ex.en: We are in charge of the policy's implementation.
ex.zh: 我們負責這項政策的執行。

ex.en: Careful planning is key to successful implementation.
ex.zh: 周詳的規劃是成功執行的關鍵。

implementation.en: the act of putting a plan or system into use

ex.en: She thought the plan was fine but impractical.
ex.zh: 她覺得這個計畫很好，但不可行。

ex.en: We all consider your idea to be impractical.
ex.zh: 我們都認為你的想法行不通。

ex.en: High heels are impractical for a long walking tour.
ex.zh: 穿高跟鞋參加長時間的徒步導覽並不實際。

impractical.en: not sensible or not likely to work in real life

imposing.zh: 雄偉的、壯觀的；令人印象深刻的

ex.en: The bank's head office is an imposing building.
ex.zh: 那家銀行的總部是一棟雄偉的建築。

ex.en: He is an imposing figure in the industry.
ex.zh: 他是業界舉足輕重的人物。

imposing.en: large and grand in a way that makes people admire it

ex.en: He told his wife not to buy on impulse.
ex.zh: 他叫太太不要衝動購物。

ex.en: I felt an impulse to cry out loud.
ex.zh: 我突然有股想大叫的衝動。

impulse.en: a sudden strong wish to do something without thinking

ex.en: Sharks are sensitive to electrical impulses as well as sound.
ex.zh: 鯊魚對電訊號和聲音都很敏感。

ex.en: Nerves send electrical impulses to the brain.
ex.zh: 神經把電訊號傳到大腦。

impulse.en: a short electrical signal that travels along a wire or nerve

ex.en: A judge must remain impartial during the trial.
ex.zh: 法官在審判期間必須保持公正。

ex.en: We need an impartial witness to tell us what happened.
ex.zh: 我們需要一位公正的證人來說明發生了什麼事。

impartial.en: fair and not supporting one side more than another

ex.en: He is an impulsive person who often buys things he doesn't need.
ex.zh: 他是個衝動的人，常常買下不需要的東西。

ex.en: It was an impulsive decision, and I regret it now.
ex.zh: 那是個衝動的決定，我現在很後悔。

impulsive.en: acting suddenly without thinking about the results

ex.en: All the events described in this story are imaginary.
ex.zh: 故事裡發生的事都是虛構出來的。

ex.en: The dragon is an imaginary creature.
ex.zh: 龍是人幻想出來的生物。

ex.en: It's just imaginary.
ex.zh: 這只是腦子想像出來的。

imaginary.en: existing only in the mind and not real

ex.en: It is very impolite of her to decline our invitation.
ex.zh: 她拒絕我們的邀請很不禮貌。

ex.en: It's impolite to stare at people.
ex.zh: 盯著人看是不禮貌的。

ex.en: They consider it impolite to disagree with someone they don't know very well.
ex.zh: 他們認為反駁不太熟的人是不禮貌的。

impolite.en: not showing good manners to other people

ex.en: The teachers are all continuing to teach despite the immense pressure.
ex.zh: 儘管壓力巨大，老師們仍然堅持教學。

ex.en: Her kindness made an immense difference in my life.
ex.zh: 她的善意對我的人生影響極大。

ex.en: They felt immense relief when their lost dog came home.
ex.zh: 走失的狗回家時，他們大大地鬆了一口氣。

ex.en: Many people think it is immoral to lie to your friends.
ex.zh: 很多人認為對朋友說謊是不道德的。

ex.en: Cheating customers is not only illegal but also immoral.
ex.zh: 欺騙顧客不只違法，也不道德。

immoral.en: not following accepted rules about what is right and good

ex.en: You guys in America can impeach your president too.
ex.zh: 你們美國人也可以彈劾總統啊。

ex.en: The president was impeached but not removed from office.
ex.zh: 總統遭到彈劾，但沒有被免職。

impeach.en: to formally accuse a public official of a serious crime in office

ex.en: We import tea from India.
ex.zh: 我們從印度進口茶葉。

ex.en: Imported cars account for less than eight percent.
ex.zh: 進口車只占不到 8%。

import.en: to bring goods in from another country, or to bring data into a program

ex.en: The imports from Asian countries have expanded recently.
ex.zh: 最近從亞洲國家的進口量不斷擴大。

ex.en: He wanted to reduce the tax on imports.
ex.zh: 他想降低進口稅。

import.en: the act of bringing goods in from abroad, or the goods themselves

ex.en: The Shanghainese people must build up Shanghai's new image.
ex.zh: 上海人必須建立上海的新形象。

ex.en: The company is trying to improve its image.
ex.zh: 這家公司正努力改善形象。

image.en: the general opinion people have about a person or group

ex.en: Images and videos are transformed into gifs and memes.
ex.zh: 影像和影片被轉換為GIF和哏。

ex.en: Choose a suitable satellite image as the base map.
ex.zh: 選擇合適的衛星圖做為底圖。

image.en: a picture or a copy of how something looks

ex.en: The contract talks reached an impasse.
ex.zh: 合約協商陷入僵局。

ex.en: Both sides proposed a review to resolve the impasse.
ex.zh: 雙方提議重新檢視，以化解僵局。

impasse.en: a situation where no progress can be made

ex.en: Please let me see your passport, also did you complete the immigration form?
ex.zh: 請出示護照。入境表格填好了嗎？

ex.en: The line at immigration was very long.
ex.zh: 入境審查的隊伍排得很長。

immigration.en: the place at an airport or border where your passport is checked

ex.en: The government is changing its immigration policy.
ex.zh: 政府正在修改移民政策。

ex.en: Immigration has changed the city over the past 50 years.
ex.zh: 過去五十年來，移民改變了這座城市。

immigration.en: the act of coming to live permanently in another country

ex.en: Lots of companies have implemented an eight-hour working day.
ex.zh: 很多公司實施每天八小時工作制。

ex.en: Our company will implement new price standards regarding this product.
ex.zh: 針對這項產品，本公司將實施新的價格標準。

ex.en: The company is starting to implement the new management system from next month.
ex.zh: 公司下個月開始推行新的管理制度。

implement.en: to start using a plan or system

ex.en: The imperial palace was open to visitors.
ex.zh: 皇宮對遊客開放。

ex.en: The museum displays many imperial treasures.
ex.zh: 博物館展示了許多皇室珍寶。

ex.en: I was impressed by her excellent English.
ex.zh: 她流利的英文讓我印象深刻。

ex.en: The teacher was impressed with his progress.
ex.zh: 老師對他的進步印象深刻。

ex.en: The man was sentenced to five years' imprisonment.
ex.zh: 那名男子被判處五年有期徒刑。

ex.en: Long imprisonment can change a person's life completely.
ex.zh: 長期的監禁可能徹底改變一個人的人生。

improved.zh: 改善、進步（improve 的過去式與過去分詞）

ex.en: Her English improved a lot after she moved abroad.
ex.zh: 她搬到國外後，英文進步了很多。

ex.en: The company improved its service by hiring more staff.
ex.zh: 這間公司增聘人手來改善服務。

ex.en: The new phone has an improved camera.
ex.zh: 這支新手機的相機經過改良。

ex.en: We saw an improved version of the app last week.
ex.zh: 上週我們看到了這款應用程式的改良版。

ex.en: The poem uses vivid imagery of the sea.
ex.zh: 這首詩用了生動的海洋意象。

ex.en: The writer's imagery helps readers picture the scene.
ex.zh: 作家的形象化描寫讓讀者能想像出場景。

ex.en: Satellite imagery shows how the forest has changed.
ex.zh: 衛星影像顯示了這片森林的變化。

ex.en: The doctor studied the imagery from the scan.
ex.zh: 醫生研究了掃描所得的影像。

ex.en: She is an imaginative child who invents new games every day.
ex.zh: 她是個很有想像力的孩子，每天都會發明新遊戲。

ex.en: The teacher gave us an imaginative way to remember the words.
ex.zh: 老師教了我們一個很有創意的記單字方法。

ex.en: The writer created an imaginative world full of talking animals.
ex.zh: 那位作家創造了一個充滿會說話動物的想像世界。

ex.en: The film mixes real history with imaginative scenes.
ex.zh: 這部電影把真實歷史和虛構的場景混合在一起。

ex.en: The little boy likes to imitate his father.
ex.zh: 小男孩喜歡模仿他的爸爸。

ex.en: Parrots can imitate human voices.
ex.zh: 鸚鵡能模仿人類的聲音。

ex.en: Young artists often imitate the style of famous painters.
ex.zh: 年輕的藝術家常會模仿著名畫家的風格。

improving.zh: 改善；進步（improve 的現在分詞）

ex.en: She is improving her English by reading every day.
ex.zh: 她每天閱讀，藉此改善英文。

ex.en: The weather is improving, so we can go out soon.
ex.zh: 天氣正在好轉，所以我們很快就可以出門了。

ex.en: He keeps improving his skills by practicing after school.
ex.zh: 他放學後練習，不斷精進自己的技巧。

improving.zh: 有教育意義的；有啟發的

ex.en: The museum offers an improving talk for young visitors.
ex.zh: 博物館為年輕的參觀者提供了一場有啟發性的導覽講解。

ex.en: She prefers improving books to light novels.
ex.zh: 她喜歡有啟發性的書，勝過輕鬆的小說。

ex.en: The dentist put an implant in place of the missing tooth.
ex.zh: 牙醫在缺牙的位置裝了一顆植牙。

ex.en: She had a hearing implant fitted last year.
ex.zh: 她去年裝了一個聽力植入物。

ex.en: Doctors implanted a small device near his heart.
ex.zh: 醫生在他的心臟附近植入了一個小裝置。

ex.en: Parents try to implant good habits in their children early.
ex.zh: 父母會試著及早在孩子心中培養好習慣。

ex.en: The king imprisoned his enemies in a tower.
ex.zh: 國王把他的敵人關在塔裡。

ex.en: People who break this law can be imprisoned for years.
ex.zh: 違反這項法律的人可能被監禁多年。

ex.en: The hospital uses medical imaging to look inside the body.
ex.zh: 醫院利用醫學影像來觀察身體內部。

ex.en: Digital imaging has made photography faster and cheaper.
ex.zh: 數位影像技術讓攝影變得更快也更便宜。

ex.en: I enjoyed the concert immensely.
ex.zh: 我非常喜歡這場演唱會。

ex.en: Your help was immensely valuable to our team.
ex.zh: 你的幫忙對我們團隊極其寶貴。

ex.en: Vaccines help the body build immunity to disease.
ex.zh: 疫苗幫助身體建立對疾病的免疫力。

ex.en: Having the illness once gave her a natural immunity.
ex.zh: 得過一次這種病讓她有了天然的免疫力。

ex.en: Diplomats have immunity from local laws.
ex.zh: 外交人員享有不受當地法律管轄的豁免權。

ex.en: The witness was given immunity in return for the truth.
ex.zh: 證人因說出實情而獲得免究。

ex.en: The new law gave fresh impetus to the recycling effort.
ex.zh: 新法律為回收工作帶來新的推動力。

ex.en: Winning the first game gave the team the impetus to keep going.
ex.zh: 贏得第一場比賽給了球隊繼續努力的動力。

ex.en: Children learn to speak through imitation.
ex.zh: 孩子們透過模仿來學說話。

ex.en: His imitation of the teacher made the whole class laugh.
ex.zh: 他模仿老師的樣子把全班逗笑了。

ex.en: This bag is an imitation, not the real thing.
ex.zh: 這個包包是仿製品，不是真品。

ex.en: The shop sells imitation pearls at a low price.
ex.zh: 這家店以低價販售仿製珍珠。

ex.en: I hope it's not an imposition to ask you for a ride.
ex.zh: 我希望請你載我一程不會太麻煩你。

ex.en: The imposition of strict rules made the students unhappy.
ex.zh: 嚴格規定的強制實施讓學生們不開心。

ex.en: The imposition of a new tax upset many shop owners.
ex.zh: 新稅的課徵讓許多店家老闆不滿。

ex.en: The imposition of fees on bags annoyed many travelers.
ex.zh: 對行李課收費用讓許多旅客不滿。

ex.en: There was an implied promise in what he said.
ex.zh: 他說的話裡含有一個隱含的承諾。

ex.en: She left without a word, but her implied meaning was clear.
ex.zh: 她一句話也沒說就離開了，但言外之意很清楚。

ex.en: The president faced an impeachment trial in the Senate.
ex.zh: 總統在參議院面臨彈劾審判。

ex.en: Lawmakers voted to begin impeachment proceedings against the judge.
ex.zh: 議員投票決定對那位法官啟動彈劾程序。

ex.en: The evidence implicated two employees in the theft.
ex.zh: 證據顯示兩名員工與竊案有牽連。

ex.en: He refused to say anything that might implicate his friends.
ex.zh: 他不肯說任何可能牽連朋友的話。

imported.zh: 進口；輸入（import 的過去式、過去分詞）

ex.en: The shop imported tea from Japan.
ex.zh: 這家店從日本進口茶葉。

ex.en: Most of the fruit is imported from overseas.
ex.zh: 大部分水果都是從海外進口的。

ex.en: Immerse the vegetables in cold water for a few minutes.
ex.zh: 把蔬菜浸在冷水裡幾分鐘。

ex.en: She immersed herself in her studies before the exam.
ex.zh: 她考前全心投入讀書。

ex.en: Living abroad helps you immerse yourself in a new language.
ex.zh: 住在國外能讓你沉浸在新的語言環境中。

ex.en: It is improper to check your phone during a funeral.
ex.zh: 在葬禮上看手機是不得體的。

ex.en: The company was fined for the improper use of customer data.
ex.zh: 這家公司因不當使用客戶資料而被罰款。

ex.en: Dark clouds warned us of the impending storm.
ex.zh: 烏雲預告了即將來臨的暴風雨。

ex.en: She felt nervous about the impending exam.
ex.zh: 她對即將到來的考試感到緊張。

ex.en: He tapped his fingers impatiently while waiting for the bus.
ex.zh: 他等公車時不耐煩地用手指敲著。

ex.en: The children waited impatiently for the cake to be ready.
ex.zh: 孩子們焦急地等著蛋糕出爐。

ex.en: The impoverished family could hardly afford food.
ex.zh: 這個貧困的家庭幾乎買不起食物。

ex.en: Aid was sent to the impoverished villages.
ex.zh: 援助物資被送往貧困的村莊。

ex.en: Her kitchen is always immaculate.
ex.zh: 她的廚房總是一塵不染。

ex.en: He wore an immaculate white shirt to the ceremony.
ex.zh: 他穿著一件潔白無瑕的襯衫參加典禮。

ex.en: The hotel room was immaculate when we arrived.
ex.zh: 我們抵達時，飯店房間乾淨得一塵不染。

ex.en: The contract implicitly allows workers to take short breaks.
ex.zh: 這份合約暗示性地允許員工短暫休息。

ex.en: He implicitly admitted his mistake by not arguing back.
ex.zh: 他沒有反駁，等於默認了自己的錯誤。

ex.en: She trusts her sister implicitly.
ex.zh: 她完全信任她的姐姐。

ex.en: The soldiers implicitly obeyed their leader.
ex.zh: 士兵們絕對服從他們的領袖。

ex.en: The singer improvised a song about the audience.
ex.zh: 歌手即興編了一首關於觀眾的歌。

ex.en: We had no hammer, so we improvised with a heavy rock.
ex.zh: 我們沒有鎚子，所以臨時拿一塊重石頭代替。

ex.en: Good cooks know how to improvise when an ingredient is missing.
ex.zh: 好廚師知道缺少材料時該怎麼臨機應變。

ex.en: Heavy snow impeded traffic all over the city.
ex.zh: 大雪阻礙了全市的交通。

ex.en: Fear of failure can impede your progress.
ex.zh: 害怕失敗可能會妨礙你的進步。

ex.en: Fallen trees impeded the rescue team's path.
ex.zh: 倒下的樹木擋住了救援隊的去路。

ex.en: The big hotel felt cold and impersonal.
ex.zh: 那間大飯店讓人覺得冷冰冰、沒有人情味。

ex.en: Her reply was formal and impersonal.
ex.zh: 她的回覆既正式又冷淡。

ex.en: Try to keep your feedback impersonal and focus on the work.
ex.zh: 回饋意見盡量客觀，專注於工作本身。

ex.en: The decision was based on impersonal market forces.
ex.zh: 這項決定是基於與個人無關的市場力量。

ex.en: He tapped his fingers on the table with impatience.
ex.zh: 他不耐煩地用手指敲著桌面。

ex.en: Her impatience grew as the line moved slowly.
ex.zh: 隊伍前進得很慢，她越來越沒耐心。

ex.en: The teacher wanted to impart her love of reading to students.
ex.zh: 老師希望把對閱讀的熱愛傳達給學生。

ex.en: Fresh herbs impart a lovely flavor to the soup.
ex.zh: 新鮮香草為這道湯增添了迷人的風味。

ex.en: Finishing the project in one day is an impossibility.
ex.zh: 一天內完成這個專案是不可能的事。

ex.en: They talked about the impossibility of changing the past.
ex.zh: 他們談到了改變過去是不可能的。

ex.en: It is improbable that it will snow in July.
ex.zh: 七月下雪是不太可能的。

ex.en: The story sounds improbable, but it is true.
ex.zh: 這個故事聽起來不太可能，但卻是真的。

ex.en: It was immature of him to shout at the referee.
ex.zh: 他對裁判大吼大叫真是幼稚。

ex.en: The fruit is still immature and too sour to eat.
ex.zh: 這水果還沒成熟，太酸了不能吃。

ex.en: Immature birds are often a different color from adults.
ex.zh: 未成年的鳥類顏色常與成鳥不同。

ex.en: Driving with impaired vision is dangerous.
ex.zh: 視力受損時開車很危險。

ex.en: His hearing was impaired after the accident.
ex.zh: 那場意外之後，他的聽力受損了。

ex.en: Lack of sleep leaves your judgment impaired.
ex.zh: 睡眠不足會使你的判斷力受損。

ex.en: The jazz band's improvisation amazed the audience.
ex.zh: 爵士樂團的即興演奏讓觀眾驚豔。

ex.en: Acting classes teach improvisation and quick thinking.
ex.zh: 表演課教你即興發揮與臨場反應。
